timeline: If you march straight toward a nuclear impact zone in 1951, how much radiation do you absorb?
But in nineteen fifty-one, the Army made six thousand five hundred soldiers march closer.
Four distinct units dug defensive trenches eleven kilometers south of ground zero.
After the blast, orders commanded them to advance straight toward the impact zone.
They marched within nine hundred meters of the crater while radiation lingered.
Officials claimed safety standards protected every single man during the test.
Yet most personnel absorbed about three roentgens of ionizing radiation exposure.
Researchers tracked their psychological reactions as they walked toward the unknown.
The military said it was safe, but the troops walked into atomic fallout.
You might think standing six miles from a nuclear bomb is far enough.
